uncited: *   **Input:** A four-dimensional data set $F$ defined on a rectilinear grid with dimensions $n_x \times n_y \times n_z \times n_t$.
The values are discrete samples at locations $x_i$.
*   **Output:** A hierarchical representation organized for spatial locality, enabling progressive visualization and out-of-core exploration.
The data is reorganized to group values belonging to the same level of detail (LOD) together.
*   $f(x_i)$ is the approximated function value obtained by quadrilinear interpolation applied to a hypercuboid in the coarser level of resolution.
Use this when adaptive spatial refinement is prioritized over the fine granularity of subdivision.
*   **Time Complexity:** Not given in the sources.
*   **When to use:** Time-varying volume data where both spatial and temporal details must be preserved at low resolutions, and progressive visualization is required.
*   **When not to use:** Static 3D data (use parent method); when adaptive spatial refinement is more critical than uniform subdivision granularity.
